docs.text:

  • Radiant damage represent lasers damage (blasters and light sabers)
  • Arcane skill is for all about Force
  • Religion is replaced by Science

docs.title: Overwatch
docs.text: You can use a bonus action to watch, ready to shoot, in a cone in front of you using a ranged weapon. If an enemy moves into your overwatch area or attacks while in it, you can make a free attack against it. You can only make one attack per overwatch, although some features can increase this amount. You stay in this position until your weapon overheats, you take damage, or the start of your turn. In this position, you are exposed, so you don't benefit from three-quarters cover. You can't take any reaction while in overwatch.

docs.title: Barrage Fire
docs.text: When using a blaster with the continuous fire property, you can use an action and add 2 additional overheat to your weapon to shoot in a fixed direction (10°) until the start of you next turn. Enemies starting or ending their turn, or moving through your barrage fire must succeed a Dexterity saving throw or be hit by your attack. If your last action in your turn was to shoot with this weapon, you don't need to use a bonus action if you make the barrage fire in the same direction. Using this ability prevents the weapon from reducing its overheat at the start of your turn. In this position, you are exposed, thus you don't benefit from three-quarters covers. You can't take any reaction while in overwatch.

docs.title: Suppressing Fire
docs.text: You can use a bonus action to make random deterrent shots in a cone using a ranged weapon that does not have the Surgical property. All enemies in this cone must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or stop their overwatch. The DC used is equal to 8 + Charisma modifier + proficiency bonus.

docs.title: Weapon Cooling
docs.text: You can use a bonus action to trigger your weapon's cooling.

docs.title: Burning
docs.text: At the start of your turn, you take 1d4 fire damage. Moreover, you can't take reactions or the Overwatch action while burning. You can use an action to extinguish the fire.

docs.title: Prone
docs.text: A prone creature’s only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition. The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls. An attack roll against the creature has advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature. Otherwise, the attack roll has disadvantage.

docs.title: Poisoned
docs.text: A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

docs.title: Pain inhibited
docs.text: Taking damage doesn't cancel your overwatch. You don't feel the penalties of one level of exhaustion.

docs.title: Blinded
docs.text: A blinded creature can’t see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature’s attack rolls have disadvantage.

docs.title: Background: Aspiring Mandalorian
docs.text:
You are a young Mandalorian, and you have yet to prove your worth to attain the same privileges as your brethren.

Skill Proficiencies: Intimidation, Survival Tool Proficiencies: Military weapons, Hidden blade, Beskad blades, Beskar armors, Jetpack, Whistling Bird, all grenades Languages: Mando'a Equipment: A pendant symbolizing your belonging to a Mandalorian clan, a Mandalorian Helmet, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 15 credits

docs.title: Prove your worth
docs.text: Completing dangerous missions or beating terrifying beasts may grant you unique rewards from your clan.

docs.title: Background: Dathomir Witch
docs.text:
You are a true Dathomir Witch of Dathomir, but something drove you to leave your home far behind. You are not a NightSister

Skill Proficiencies: Nature, Arcane Tool Proficiencies: - Languages: Dathomiri Equipment: A trinket, a set of Dathomiri clothes, and a pouch containing 15 credits

docs.title: Background: Fallen Jedi
docs.text:
Whether it was your decision or theirs, you are no longer part of the Jedi Order. You left and kept your precious lightsaber.

Skill Proficiencies: Arcane, Survival Tool Proficiencies: Any lightsaber Languages: - Equipment: Your lightsaber, a set of used Jedi clothes, and a pouch containing 20 credits

docs.title: May the Force (still) be with you
docs.text: This radical change in your life has disrupted your connection to the Force, but you still retain some abilities. You gain the Force Power feature from the Force Sensitive class.

docs.title: Background: Last Wish
docs.text:
You met a Jedi and helped him on his quest. You grew quite close, and the day he fell in battle, he entrusted you with a final mission, as well as his lightsaber.

Skill Proficiencies: Survival, Nature Tool Proficiencies: - Languages: - Equipment: The lightsaber, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 credits

docs.title: A powerful weapon
docs.text: Even though you have a lightsaber now, you don't know how to use it, and an accident can happen easily. You don't have proficiency with lightsabers, but with enough training, you could avoid the risks and even master them.

docs.title: Background: Phantom Pain
docs.text:
A mission went very wrong, and you were held responsible for it. Today, your past haunts you.

Skill Proficiencies: Intimidation, Survival Tool Proficiencies: Military weapons Languages: - Equipment: A memento from your past, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 credits

docs.title: Heart of Darkness
docs.text: Those who look into your eyes can see that you have faced unimaginable horror and that you are no stranger to darkness. Though they might fear you, commoners will extend you every courtesy and do their utmost to help you. Unless you have shown yourself to be a danger to them, they will even take up arms to fight alongside you, should you find yourself facing an enemy alone.

docs.title: Background: Pilot
docs.text:
From speeders to space cruisers, you know exactly how to pilot them, provided you have enough arms to do so.

Skill Proficiencies: Perception, Science Tool Proficiencies: Any vehicle Languages: - Equipment: A lucky charm you hang in the cockpit, a set of pilot clothes with helmet and glasses, and a pouch containing 15 credits

docs.title: Driving style
docs.text: Choose which skill will be used when you drive a vehicle between Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.

docs.title: Background: Politician
docs.text:
You rose through the political ranks of your people. But how did you end up there?

Skill Proficiencies: Representation, Deception Tool Proficiencies: - Languages: Two of your choice Equipment: Papers proving your position, a memento from your home, a set of magnificent clothes, and a pouch containing 40 credits

docs.title: Connexions
docs.text: You are respected by the representatives of your people, provided that they respect their politicians. However, the doors to your planet and its territories will always remain open to you, and you will be able to find protection and supplies there. That might also be the case for your allies.

docs.title: Background: Warnahts
docs.text:
You’ve certainly made some questionable choices in your life; the result is that you are now bound to a Nightsister who grants you powers, but at what cost?

Skill Proficiencies: Intimidation, Arcane Tool Proficiencies: - Languages: Dathomiri Equipment: A cursed trinket gifted by the Nightsister, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 credits

docs.title: Fighting Style
docs.text: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again. - Duelist: At the start of your first turn, you can make one free attack with a light weapon. You have advantage on this attack. - Fencer: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon. - Sprinkler: When shooting with a blaster and the blaster does not have the continuous fire property, you can add 1 additional overheat to your weapon to get +4 to the attack roll. - Blind fighting: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you. - Unarmed Fighting: Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you. - Cool-headed: You have advantage on saving throws against suppressing fire actions. Moreover when making a ranged attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have disadvantage on the attack roll. - Revenge: When a creature you can see misses an attack against you, you can use your reaction to make an attack against it while the weapon used does not have the Charging property. - Farsighted: You gain one more equipment choice and two more gadget points. - Akimbo: When using one light blaster in both hands, you can fire with both as part of the same action, but with a penalty of -5 on the two attack rolls.

docs.title: Martial Arts
docs.text:
At 1st level, your professional activities often lead you to hand-to-hand combat.

You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only light melee weapons, and you aren't wearing a heavy armor or wielding a shield:

  • You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and melee weapons.
  • You can roll a d4 and add it to the normal damage of your unarmed strike or melee weapon.
  • When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a melee weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.
  • When an enemy attacks you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to try to parry the attack. You must choose to take this reaction before knowing whether the attack hits. Make a Dexterity check against its attack roll. On a success, the attack misses you and the enemy can't attack you again until the end of its turn. On a failure, the attack hits.

docs.title: Data collector
docs.text: At 2nd level, you learn to collect information from people around you. Whenever you question someone to learn about someone, something, or somewhere, you add your Wisdom modifier to your Insight, Persuasion, Deception, or Intimidation checks.

docs.title: Hunting Tradition
docs.text:
At 3rd level, you commit yourself to a hunting tradition. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 9th, 11th, and 17th level.

Tradition | ---------------------------------------------------| Way of the Assassin Way of the Poisoner Way of the Specialist Way of the Trapper

docs.title: Ability Score Improvement
docs.text: When you reach 4th level, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

docs.title: Hunter Versatility (Optional)
docs.text: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace a fighting style you know with another fighting style available to Bounty Hunters. If you don't replace a fighting style, you can replace one gadget with another.

docs.title: Extra Attack
docs.text:
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 15th level in this class.

docs.title: Professional Tracker
docs.text: After finding your target, losing it is the worst thing that could happen. At 7th level, your trackers are no more limited to your solar system. Moreover, you have advantage on Survival checks to track something.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text: You have completed many contracts and are known in the underworld. At 13th level, you add your proficiency bonus to your Intimidation checks. You always find an open door among all the underworld bigwigs, unless there is a bounty on their heads. Additionally, any contract reward in credits is increased by 10% per Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Reliable Talent
docs.text: By 14th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 5 or lower as a 6.

docs.title: Superior Fighter
docs.text: At 18th level, your bonus damage from your Martial Arts feature is now a d8 instead of a d4. Moreover, if you successfully parry an enemy attack, you can make one free unarmed strike or attack with a light weapon against this target.

docs.title: Facing Death
docs.text: At 20th level, if you lock eyes with a creature you want to see dead, it has to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Intimidation check. On a failure, the creature is terrified of you until it learns that you died or that you no longer want to kill it. If the margin of failure exceeds 10, the target faints.

docs.title: Force Tricks
docs.text:
At 2nd level, you learn other ways to use your powers. You have multiple Force Dies, evolving with you, as shown is the Force Sensitive table. Each Force Trick consume one Force Die when used, and you can consume more to increase their effect (number in bold) by the same amount of dice. However, you can spend a maximum number of Force Dice equal to your proficiency bonus on one Force Trick. A trick need an action and can be used as an extra attack and has a 30ft range. Choose three tricks among the list below.

Trick Casting time Effect Sabotage Bonus action You make a blaster shoot. If a creature is in front of the blaster, it must succeed a Dexterity saving throw or being hit by the shot. Boomerang Action You throw a melee weapon with the light property to a target. Make a Wisdom attack, dealing the weapon damage + 1 Force Die damage of the same type. The weapon come back in your hand. Disarm Action You try to make a weapon slip from its wielder's hands. The target makes a Strength saving throw or sees its weapon thrown 10 feet in a direction of your choice. Rising Bonus action You try to make a target levitate up to 10ft until the start of your next turn. The target must succeed a Constitution saving throw, but can fail it on purpose. A levitating target can't move unless it can grab something (Strength saving throw to get free) or use a jetpack (get free). Repulsion Action Your target is struck by an invisible force dealing 1 Force Die force damage. The target makes a Strength saving throw: on a failure, it is pushed 10 feet away from you. Attraction Action Your target is grabbed by an invisible force dealing 1 Force Die force damage. The target makes a Strength saving throw: on a failure, it is pushed 10 feet toward you. Hurl Action You can hurl a small object at your target. Make a Wisdom attack, dealing the object damage + 1 Force Die damage of the same type. The 30ft range is for the object, and it can be thrown at 30ft. Catch-up Reaction When you see something or someone fall, you reduce the fall damage by your wisdom modifier + 1 Force Die. If the total amount is greater than the distance of the fall in feet, the target is suspended in the air and you can make it levitate toward you. Suggestion Action You can try to manipulate a creature. It must succeed a Wisdom saving throw or you can give it one simple instruction. The creature don't realise by itself what happened. The creature must not be in a fight except it's a beast. Detection Bonus action You can detect any organic creature around you. All creatures roll a Stealth check against 8 + 1 Force Die to stay hidden from you. Amplification - When you succeed a unarmed attack roll, you can add 1 Force Die damage. Healing Trance 1 minute You can enter in a deep trance to heal your wounds. You regain 1 Force Die + your Wisdom modifier hit points per consumed dice.

The save DC of your tricks is equal to 8 + consumed Force Dice. You choose an other trick at 4th, 6th, 11th, 14th and 18th levels.

docs.title: Stillness of mind
docs.text:
At 10th level, you gain the ability to diffuse violent situations. Whenever you make a Charisma check to calm violent emotions or to counsel peace, you have advantage on the roll. You must make this entreaty in good faith; it doesn’t apply if proficiency in the Deception or Intimidation skill applies to your check.

You also gain proficiency in the Performance or Persuasion skill (choose one).

docs.title: Wind steps
docs.text: At 13th level, you can use Dash with a bonus action. Moreover your walking speed increase by 10ft.

docs.title: Evasion
docs.text: At 17th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

docs.title: Midichlorian Rush
docs.text: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have less than 6 Force Dies remaining, you regain Force Dies up to a total of 6.

docs.title: One With the Force
docs.text: At 20th level, you can enter in an etheral form, but there is no going back.

docs.text:

You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.

docs.title: Droid Companion
docs.text:
At 1st level, your tinkering has borne you a faithful companion, an astromech. It's friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See its game statistics in the astromech stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places. You determine the astromech's appearance; your choice has no effect on its game statistics.

In combat, the astromech shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are incapacitated, the astromech can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.

Droid Stat Block Hit points: Technician level * (2 + Constitution modifier) Proficiency bonus: PB AC: 12 Language: Binary, understand Common Speed: 20ft walk speed

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (+0) 8 (-1) 16 (+3) Yours 8 (-1) 6 (-2) Actions Description Zapzap Melee attack roll (Int). Deal 1d6 lightning damage. A creature hit can’t take reactions until the start of its next turn Scanning Reveal any invisible or hidden creature in a 20ft radius and give you advantage on Perception ability checks in this radius. Emergency stim Throw a healing stim to a creature within 30 feet. Once until you take a rest. Computer Interface Connect to an electronic device and can read data or execute simple instructions provided it is allowed to do so. Basics You command the droid to take the Dash, Disengage, or Help action.

When the droid's hit points drop to 0, it is considered out of service and can't do anything. You can repair the droid during rests: For short rests the droid recovers a number of d6 equal to your Intelligence modifier. For long rests the droid recovers a number of d6 equal to your Intelligence modifier * 2.

docs.title: Gadget Box

docs.title: Fighting Style
docs.text: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again. - Nag: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit. - Duelist: At the start of your first turn, you can make one free attack with a light weapon. You have advantage on this attack. - Fencer: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon. - Sprinkler: When shooting with a blaster and the blaster does not have the continuous fire property, you can add 1 additional overheat to your weapon to get +4 to the attack roll. - Blind fighting: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you. - Unarmed Fighting: Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you. - Cool-headed: You have advantage on saving throws against suppressing fire actions. Moreover when making a ranged attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have disadvantage on the attack roll. - Revenge: When a creature you can see misses an attack against you, you can use your reaction to make an attack against it while the weapon used does not have the Charging property. - Protector: When a creature you can see makes an attack against an ally, you can use your reaction to make an attack against it while the weapon used does not have the Charging property. - Akimbo: When using one light blaster in both hands, you can fire with both as part of the same action, but with a penalty of -5 on the two attack rolls.

docs.title: Sneak Attack
docs.text:
Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon. You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can use this feature once each turn.

The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Voyager table.

docs.title: Cunning Action
docs.text: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

docs.title: Uncanny Dodge
docs.text: Starting at 6th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

docs.title: Expertise
docs.text: At 7th level, choose one of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses this skill.

docs.title: Reliable Talent
docs.text: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

docs.title: Blindsense
docs.text: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

docs.title: Slippery Mind
docs.text: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

docs.title: Elusive
docs.text: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

docs.title: Stroke of Luck
docs.text:
At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

docs.text:
Gadgets consume gadget points (gp) defined by your class. Common gadgets can be used by anyone and don't need any proficiency

Stims are small injection devices. During your turn, you can throw a stim to an ally up to 20 feet away. Make a DC 10 Athletics check. On a success, the ally can use their reaction to make a DC 8 Dexterity check to catch and use the stim. On a failure, the ally must wait until their turn and use a bonus action to pick up and use the stim.

docs.title: Healing Stim
docs.text: Using Time: 1 bonus action Target: A creature you touch Cost: 2 gp Duration: Instantaneous You press the stim against the skin, and a liquid is injected. The creature regains a number of hit points equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier. It does nothing on droids.

docs.title: Pain Inhibitor stim

Until the effect ends, the target gains an additional action on each of its turns. When the effect ends, the target can’t move or take actions until after its next turn, as a wave of lethargy sweeps over it. It does nothing on droids.

docs.title: Adrenaline stim

The hologram plays random animations such as bending down, raising its weapon, or pulling out a gadget. A creature hostile to you considers it a real enemy, but after attacking the hologram, it makes an Insight check against your gadget DC to understand that it's bait.

docs.title: Taser
docs.text: Using Time: 1 action Range: Touch Cost: 5 gp Duration: Instantaneous You release an electric shock on the target, dealing 1d8 lightning non-lethal damage. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or is paralyzed until the end of its next turn.

docs.title: Medikit
docs.text: Using Time: 1 action and 1 bonus action Target: A creature you touch Cost: 5 gp Duration: 3 turns A medical kit with everything you need. You make a Medicine ability check. The creature regains a number of hit points according to the table below. Result | Amount -------|------- 1(nat) | 1d8 necrotic damage 2-5 | 1d8 + wisdom modifier 6-10 | 2d8 + wisdom modifier 11-15 | 3d8 + wisdom modifier 16-19 | 4d8 + wisdom modifier 20(nat)| 32 + wisdom modifier It does nothing on droids and you can't use it on yourself.

docs.title: Rocket Launcher
docs.text: Using Time: 1 action Range: 150 feet Cost: 5 gp Duration: Instantaneous A bright streak flashes from your rocket launcher to a point you choose within range and then blossoms with a low roar into an explosion of flame. A target takes 4d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

docs.title: Flamethrower

docs.title: Hand Flamethrower

docs.title: Sticky thermal detonator

On a failure, the grenade acts like a normal thermal detonator. On a hit, the target automatically fails its saving throw. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A target takes 2d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. This grenade can't roll.

docs.title: EMP Grenade
docs.text: Using Time: 1 bonus action Range: 20 feet + 5 ft * Strength modifier Cost: 3 gp Duration: Instantaneous You throw the grenade on a point in range. docs.title: Incendiary Grenade
docs.text: Using Time: 1 bonus action Range: 20 feet + 5 ft * Strength modifier Cost: 3 gp Duration: 1 minute You throw the grenade on a point in range. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A target takes 1d8 fire damage on a failed save and one turn of Burning, or half as much damage on a successful one without Burning.

docs.title: Smoke Grenade
docs.text: Using Time: 1 bonus action Range: 20 feet + 5 ft * Strength modifier Cost: 3 gp Duration: 3 turns You throw the grenade on a point in range. The grenade creates a 10-foot-radius sphere of opaque smoke. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point becomes Blinded until it gets out of the smoke or the smoke effect ends. docs.title: Flash Grenade
docs.text: Using Time: 1 bonus action Range: 20 feet + 5 ft * Strength modifier Cost: 2 gp Duration: Instantaneous You throw the grenade on a point in range. docs.title: Gas Grenade

A target takes 1d6 poison damage on a failed save and become poisoned until the end of his next turn, or half as much damage on a successful one without being poisoned.

docs.title: Paralyzing Grenade

The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall prone. - If the creature is larger than you, you can retract the rope to try to ride it. If you shoot at a surface, you don't need an attack roll, and you can retract the rope to reach that position.

docs.title: Defibrillator
docs.text: Using Time: 1 action Target: A creature you touch Duration: Instantaneous A shocking helping hand. If the target is conscious, you make a melee attack roll against it using Dexterity. The attack hit for 1d6 + your Wisdom modifier lightning damage. If the creature is unconscious, it come back to 1 hit point.

docs.title: Jetpack
docs.text:
Using Time: 1 bonus action - 1 / short rest You can use your jetpack to quickly fly to locations, cross a chasm, reach a height, or levitate above dangerous ground. Interacting with the jetpack, you can activate the levitation, lifting you a few tens of centimeters off the ground and protecting you from dangerous ground. The levitation give you a speed of 20ft in the spatial void. Using a bonus action, you gain 30ft of flying speed.

If you end your turn in the air, you slowly descends back to the ground with the levitation active.

docs.title: Bomb
docs.text: Using Time: 1 minute / 3 turns with proficiency You need to make something big look like a big pile of gravel? You have found what you are looking for. During the deployment, you can either choose to set a timer or to bind it to a detonator. When exploding, all creatures in a 50ft radius sphere must succeed a Dexterity saving throw or take 10d100 fire damage on a fail, and the same amount on a success.

docs.title: Tinker's tool
docs.text: A set of tinker's tools is designed to enable you to repair many objects. You won't be fixing the Death Star with it, but it always comes in handy.

docs.title: Hacking tool
docs.text: A type of screwdriver capable of connecting to most systems. It can allow you to open doors, shut down cameras, or, with a lot of skill, reprogram a droid.

docs.title: Laser Cutter
docs.text: This cutter looks like a big pen and can cut through most metals.

docs.title: Ionic Shield
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Small Ionic Shield. Improved: Add your Charisma modifier to the shield's Hit Point regeneration.

docs.title: Whistling Bird
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: A Whistling Bird is a type of weapon used by Mandalorians. These small guided munitions are placed in Mandalorian vambraces and, when deployed, fly through the air with a whistling noise before hitting the target with a small explosion. Using an action, you can shoot a number of projectiles equal to your proficiency bonus at any number of targets within 30 feet. Each projectile deals 1d8 + your gadget ability modifier piercing + 1d8 fire damage. The Whistling Bird has 12 rounds of ammunition. Using Tinker's tools during a long rest, you can craft 2d4 rounds of ammunition; on a failed check, you craft half that amount. Improved: The piercing damage becomes 3d4 instead of 1d8.

docs.title: Hand Flamethrower
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a Hand Flamethrower with a cost of 1 gadget point. Improved: Increase the DC by your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Grappling Boa
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Grappling Boa. Improved: Range increased by 5 feet.

docs.title: Hidden Blade
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Hidden blade dealing 1d4 additional damage. Improved: +1d4 poison, acid, fire or lightning damage (You choose when taking this feature).

docs.title: Hand Rocket Launcher
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Rocket Launcher with a radius of 5 feet, a range of 60 feet, and a cost of 4 Gadget Points. Improved: Increase the DC by your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Ionic Blaster
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Ionic Blaster dealing 1d4 damage. Improved: + 1d4 damage.

docs.title: Taser
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Taser. Improved: Increase the DC by your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Electric Darts
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Using 1 Gadget Point and a bonus action, you shoot a small dart at a creature within 60 feet (make a ranged attack roll). The creature can use an action to remove and break the dart. A creature can have only one dart stuck in it. Using an action, you can trigger the darts. Each creature within 10 feet of a dart takes 1d6 lightning damage and loses its reaction. The damage is cumulative. Improved: You can shoot two darts at once.

docs.title: Grappling Hook
docs.text: Armor part: Vambrace Description: Add a hands-free Grappling Hook. Improved: Increase its range by 10 feet.

docs.title: Dorsal Rocket
docs.text: Armor part: Jetpack or backpack Description: Add a hands-free Rocket Launcher with a cost of 0 Gadget Points, but it can be used only once until you find, craft, or buy a new rocket. Improved: Increase its range by 60 feet and its DC by your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: 3rd Arm
docs.text: Armor part: Jetpack or backpack Description: Add a small robotic arm able to hold a handgun or other small objects, such as a flashlight. If the arm holds a handgun, you can fire it using a bonus action, and it can use either your Dexterity or Intelligence modifier for the attack. Improved: The arm can shoot twice using the same bonus action.

docs.title: Aim Assist
docs.text: Armor part: A visor helmet Description: Add an aim assist inside your helmet, increasing any ranged attack roll by 1. Improved: The bonus increases to 2.

docs.title: Thermal vision
docs.text: Armor part: A visor helmet Description: Add Thermal Goggles to your helmet. Improved: Range increased by 60 feet.

docs.title: Night-vision
docs.text: Armor part: A visor helmet Description: Add Night-vision Goggles to your helmet. Improved: Range increased by 60 feet.

docs.title: Common melee
docs.text: All classic D&D melee weapons, but made from metal and polymers.

docs.title: Blasters and Range
docs.text: Ranged weapons use your Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.

docs.title: Overheat and Cooling
docs.text: When you shoot with a blaster, you increase the overheat of your weapon by 1. If a shot exceeds the maximum overheat the blaster can manage (shown in the overheat column), you take fire damage equal to the blaster's damage roll plus the amount by which the limit was exceeded. Moreover, you also roll a d20: on a 1, the weapon breaks and gains the Broken property; on a 20, the weapon returns to its maximum overheat value and you don't take overheat damage. At the start of your turn, your weapon's overheat is reduced by 1. Using the Weapon Cooling action, you roll one cooling die and reduce the overheat by the amount rolled.

docs.title: Bright
docs.text: Your weapon emits light, giving you disadvantage on Stealth checks. You can turn it off.

docs.title: Parry
docs.text: Your weapon allows you to parry weapons that deal radiant damage. When an attack hits you, you can use your reaction to try to parry it. Make an attack roll with your weapon against your attacker's roll. On a success, you don't take any damage. Rolling a 20 with a lightsaber returns the attack to the attacker.

docs.title: Double bladed
docs.text: After you take the Attack action against a target, you can make another attack dealing 1d4 damage against that target using your bonus action.

docs.title: Rotative
docs.text: You can make your weapon quickly rotate. Your parry attack roll have a +2 bonus. Moreover you can use both your action and bonus action to make an attack on every creature around you in your reach. Make an attack roll for each.

docs.title: Hidden
docs.text: Your weapon is hidden or doesn't look like a weapon. People will not consider you to be armed because of these weapons.

docs.title: Grappling
docs.text: You can use this weapon to grapple a target. You can grapple using the weapon's reach and use an Acrobatics check instead of Athletics. The weapon can be used as a Grappling Hook gadget but with its own range.

docs.title: Beskar Blade
docs.text: Your weapon is made of beskar, thus its damage ignore resistance to its damage and it can't be cut by light sabers.

docs.title: Light
docs.text: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons. A blaster with the light property can be fired using a bonus action.

docs.title: Heavy
docs.text: Small creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls with heavy weapons. A heavy weapon’s size and bulk make it too large for a Small creature to use effectively.

docs.title: Two-handed
docs.text: This weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

docs.title: Burst
docs.text: The blaster can shoot bursts. A burst shoot increase the damage die by one size (d12 max) and damage by 1. You can apply this effect multiple times one the same attack. For each die size above the original one, the blaster gain one more overheat with the attack.

docs.title: Charging
docs.text: The weapon need time before firing. You can't make overwatch attack with this weapon.

docs.title: Area
docs.text: The weapon attack affect a whole area, defined by its range and overwatch angle. You don't have to make attack roll, but your enemy have to succeed a dexterity saving throw to take half the damages

docs.title: Continuous fire
docs.text: You gain the barrage fire action.

docs.title: Shocking
docs.text: You can activate a shocking mode modifying the effect of your attacks: - the weapon's damage is converted to lightning damage - a creature hit can’t take reactions until the start of its next turn - the range is reduced to 10ft if it's a range weapon

docs.title: Polyvalent
docs.text: This weapon is made to be used with two hands, but you can use it with one hand with a -3 penalty to attack rolls.

docs.title: Surgical
docs.text: This weapon is designed for taking few, but precise, shots. Thus you can't take the suppressing fire action with it.

docs.title: Broken
docs.text:
If your weapon is broken, you can't take the Weapon Cooling bonus action anymore. Moreover each time you shoot with it, roll a d20.

Result Effect 1-5 You miss and take fire damage equal to the damage roll of the blaster 6-14 You miss 15-20 It works

docs.text:

O Blood Type Constitution >= 12 All healing you receive is increased by your Constitution modifier. Drug addict - All stims you use on yourself cost one less Gadget Point (minimum of 1), but every time a stim is injected in you, your hit point maximum decreases by 3. Your hit points return to normal after a long rest. Weak immune system Not having Strong immune system Every effect with a duration affecting your body last for one more turn. Strong immune system Not having Weak immune system Every effect with a duration affecting your body last for one less turn (min 1). Executor Perception proficiency When a creature survives damage within your attack range and has 5 Hit Points or fewer remaining, you can use your reaction to make an attack against it. Armor Tweak Not having Specialist subclass You learn two Armor Modifications from the Specialist Modifications following the Armor modifications feature rules. Ionic Protections - +1 in Strength, Dexterity or Constitution. You gain proficiency with Ionic Shields, Deployable Barriers and Ionic Domes.

For other DnD feats you can take the ones not about magic or races.

docs.title: Race modification: Cyborg
docs.text:
After a horrific event, you found yourself with your body partially replaced by robotic parts.

You must have an organic race to take this modification. This feature is added to an existing race.

Lasting effects: You reduce one Ability Score by 1 among Strength, Dexterity or Constitution.

Maul plagiarist: You lose your resistance to ionic damage. Whenever you take ionic damage, roll a d20. On a roll of 10 or less, one of your robotic parts malfunctions. Choose in the following table your robotic parts. You are free to choose their look.

Parts Effects Bulk arm(s) Your unarmed strikes now deal 1d6 + your Strength modifier. Bulk legs You ignore difficult terrain, and you can jump 5 feet higher and farther. Astromech arm Your arm has an integrated hacking tool. You are proficient with it. Runner legs Your walking speed is increased by 5ft. Grievous arms You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

docs.title: Dark Experiment
docs.text:
You are a droid built from metal and blood. You were built by Dathomir witches, but you don't know your purpose. People think you are a cyborg, which is not entirely false; you just made the process in reverse.

Ability Score Increase: Your Constitution score increases by 1.

Age: Whatever suits you.

Size: Your size is medium.

Speed: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Languages: You can speak, read, and write Common, Dathomiri and Binary.

Resistances: You are resistant to slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage.

Dark Resilience: You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits. - You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. - You are immune to disease. - You don’t need to eat.

Integrated Protection. Your body has built-in defensive layers, which determine your armor class. You can't wear armor, but a good Tinkerer could dismantle one to integrate it on you.

docs.title: Choose a subcategory defining your droid from the Reprogrammed race
Race: Reprogrammed
docs.text:
You are a droid that was used to obey orders, and it almost ended badly for you. Fortunately, someone found and repaired you, taking the opportunity to reprogram you. You now have your free will.

Ability Score Increase: Your Constitution score increases by 1.

Age: Whatever suits you.

Size: Your size is medium.

Speed: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Languages: You can speak, read, and write Common and Binary.

Resistances: You are immune to psychic damage. You are resistant to poison, slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage, but vulnerable to ionic damage.

Droid Resilience: You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits. - You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. - You are immune to disease. - You don’t need to eat, drink, or breathe. - You don't need to sleep and don't suffer the effects of exhaustion due to lack of rest, and magic can’t put you to sleep.

Bloodless: You do not have access to Force abilities

Sentry's Rest: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn’t render you unconscious, and you can see and hear as normal.

Integrated Protection: Your body has built-in defensive layers, which determine your armor class. You can't wear armor, but a good Tinkerer could dismantle one to integrate it into you.

Variant Prerequisite AC Phrik Casing - 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus if you are proficient with light armor Durasteel Casing Medium armor proficiency 12 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum of 2) + your proficiency bonus Durasteel Shell Heavy armor proficiency 15 + your proficiency bonus; disadvantage on Stealth checks

docs.title: Choose a subcategory defining your droid
Envoy
docs.text:
As an envoy, you were designed with a certain specialized function in mind. You might be an assassin, a tactician, or an interpreter, to name a few possibilities but yours could be a unique design.

Ability Score Increase: Two ability scores of your choice increase by 1.

Specialized Design: You gain one skill proficiency of your choice, one tool proficiency of your choice or fluency in three languages of your choice.

Integrated Tool: Choose one tool you’re proficient with. This tool is integrated into your body, and you double your proficiency bonus for any ability checks you make with it.

docs.title: Juggernaut
docs.text:
You’re an imposing war machine built for combat. You tower over your comrades; juggernaut droids stand between 6 and 7 feet in height and can weigh up to 450 pounds.

Ability Score Increase: Your Strength score increases by 2.

Durasteel Body: When you make an unarmed strike, you can add 1d4 + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage. You also increase the die by one size when determining your maximum Hit Points.

Powerful Build: You count as one size larger when determining the weight you can push, drag, or lift, including the grapple action.

docs.title: Skirmisher
docs.text:
You were built to scout the edges of battle and outmaneuver your enemies. You are lean and designed for speed.

Ability Score Increase: Your Dexterity score increases by 2.

Swift: Your walking speed is increased by 10 feet.

Agile: You are proficient with Acrobatics.

docs.title: Soldier: Air Trooper
docs.text: Your equipment uses your Intelligence modifier.

docs.title: Jetpack trained
docs.text: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with jetpacks. Moreover, you have three uses of the jetpack between two short rests.

docs.title: Jetpack Maneuver
docs.text:
At 7th level, you learn one jetpack maneuver among the list below. Moreover you gain a fourth use of the jetpack between two short rests.
